ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, it is known that $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, and $AB=8C$, $D$ is a point on $\odot O$, $OC\parallel BD$, intersecting $AD$ at point $E$, and $BC$ is connected, $\angle CBD=30^\circ$. Calculate the area of the shaded region in the diagram (the result should retain $\pi$).
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\[ \text{Solution: Connect } OD, \]
\[ \because \angle CBD = \angle OBC = 30^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore \angle BOD = 60^\circ, \]
\[ \because OB = OD, \]
\[ \therefore \triangle BOD \text{ is an equilateral triangle}, \]
\[ \therefore \text{Area of the shaded region} = \text{Area of sector } BOD - \text{Area of } \triangle BOD = \frac{60\pi \times 4^2}{360} - \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 4 = \boxed{\frac{8}{3}\pi -4\sqrt{3}}. \]

阴影面积=扇形 BOD 面积-三角形 BOD 面积。扇形面积为 (60/360)π×4²=8π/3。三角形 BOD 的面积为 (1/2)×4×4×sin60°=4√3。因此阴影面积为 8π/3-4√3。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, it is known that $AB$ is the diameter of $\odot O$, and $AB=8C$, $D$ is a point on $\odot O$, $OC\parallel BD$, intersecting $AD$ at point $E$, and $BC$ is connected, $\angle CBD=30^\circ$. Calculate the area of the shaded region in the diagram (the result should retain $\pi$).
raw_record.answer:
\[ \text{Solution: Connect } OD, \]
\[ \because \angle CBD = \angle OBC = 30^\circ, \]
\[ \therefore \angle BOD = 60^\circ, \]
\[ \because OB = OD, \]
\[ \therefore \triangle BOD \text{ is an equilateral triangle}, \]
\[ \therefore \text{Area of the shaded region} = \text{Area of sector } BOD - \text{Area of } \triangle BOD = \frac{60\pi \times 4^2}{360} - \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 4 = \boxed{\frac{8}{3}\pi -4\sqrt{3}}. \]
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure there is a circle, AB is a horizontal diameter, O is on AB and is marked as the center of the circle; C is on the upper-left arc, and D is on the upper-right arc. In the figure AD, CB, CO, and BD are connected, and the intersection of AD and CO is marked as E. The gray shaded area on the right near B and D is the small circular segment area enclosed by chord BD and the minor arc BD.
Reasoning: The problem gives AB=8, therefore the radius OB=OD=4. It is known that OC ∥ BD, and ∠CBD=30°. Because BD is parallel to OC, ∠CBD is equal to the angle between CB and CO, that is, ∠BCO=30°. Also because OB and OC are both radii, OB=OC, triangle OBC is an isosceles triangle, so ∠OBC=∠BCO=30°, thus ∠BOC=120°. Since chord BD is drawn from B parallel to OC, corresponding to the center of the circle gives ∠BOD=60°. Connect OD, then OB=OD=4, and the included angle ∠BOD=60°, so triangle BOD is an equilateral triangle. The shaded area is equal to the area of the 60° sector BOD minus the area of triangle BOD: sector area = (60/360)·π·4² = 8π/3; area of equilateral triangle BOD = (√3/4)·4² = 4√3. Therefore the shaded area = 8π/3 - 4√3.
